items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: And Howard Nemerov was my comp teacher, the great poet

ctx.x: You know on that kind of thing you’re either going to get an A or you’re going to get a zero.

I was a freshman you know, I was a freshman, my God. I was 18 years old, What did I know? But yeah for me it was a good background obviously to be well read. And I took it for granted that I was going to study English literature, which I did. I took I think all the courses in English literature that Hamilton offered at that time except Shakespeare which I figured I knew enough about anyway. And Howard Nemerov was my comp teacher, the great poet, well certainly well known poet, now dead. Howard was at Hamilton for…
I was thinking, if I do the math right, according to your birthdate, you almost would have been draftable at the end of World War II, right?
